gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Oxanium draws every stroke with one fixed nib, sharp and unbroken. Its high x-height makes the lowercase loom large, while Noto Sans Elbasan answers with large, open-mouthed letters whose terminals never pinch shut.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-carrois-gothic: Loud, scattered letters with real attitude. Paprika commands the top with lowercase that fills the line like capitals, while Carrois Gothic, the plain sans below, does its best work with a tall x-height guide and generous c opening.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Big personality, loose and shouting. Paprika's lowercase fills the line like capitals, so shrinking it wastes that presence, while Noto Sans Kannada keeps a gentle step up to capitals and s curves open at both ends.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-funnel-sans: Wide-striding display letters with a lazy swagger. Revalia stands tall and spaced out, while Funnel Sans, drawn as if by a round-tipped pen, holds stroke widths steady; that gap between loud and low is the pair's best trait.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Showy, spread-out letters with a slow, easy gait. Revalia stretches wide with an open-bottomed g, while Noto Sans Bengali, a sans, stays modest, its capitals barely above lowercase and its letter mouths open.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Bold letters strolling with room to spare. Revalia's open-curled g and wide stride set against Noto Sans Kaithi's open e channel make the biggest difference: one lounges, the other fills the line like capitals.
